## Función principal
- Reemplaza al API de OpenAI sin cambiar tu código
- Decide automáticamente qué modelo usar según categorías: coding, reasoning, multilingüe, etc.
- Prefiere local (Ollama) sobre cloud cuando las puntuaciones son iguales (gratis y privado)

## Endpoints disponibles
- `/local/v1` — solo modelos locales (Ollama)
- `/cloud/v1` — solo modelos en la nube (Groq, NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter)
- `/v1` — híbrido con fallback automático

## ¿Cómo funciona?
1. Tú defines rankings YAML en `rankings/local.yaml` y `rankings/cloud.yaml`
2. El router lee esos rankings y elige el mejor modelo por categoría
3. Tu app llama como si fuera OpenAI, pero usa el modelo que tú definiste como "mejor"

## Ejemplo de uso
```bash
curl http://localhost:9002/local/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "best:coding", ...}'
```

actions.result:
# local-model-router

An OpenAI-compatible HTTP proxy that routes requests to the **best available LLM** — local (Ollama) or cloud (NVIDIA NIM, Groq, OpenRouter) — based on per-category benchmarks you own and control.

```bash
# ask for the best model for coding — router decides, you don't change a line of code
curl http://localhost:9002/local/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "best:coding", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a binary search in Python."}]}'
```

---

## Why

Running LLMs locally is free and private. Cloud models are faster and stronger. Most tools make you pick one. This router lets you use both through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with rankings you built from your own benchmarks.

**Key properties:**
- Drop-in replacement for the OpenAI API — no code changes in your apps
- Three endpoint families: local-only, cloud-only, hybrid with fallback
- Rankings are YAML files in the repo — you control who's "best"
- Local is always preferred over cloud when scores are equivalent (cost $0 vs latency)

---

## Architecture

```
your app  →  local-model-router (port 9002)
                     │
          ┌──────────┼──────────┐
          │          │          │
      /local      /cloud      /v1
     (Ollama)  (NIM/Groq/  (hybrid)
                OpenRouter)
          │          │          │
      rankings/  rankings/  tries both
      local.yaml cloud.yaml in order
```

```
router/
├── server.py       FastAPI app — three endpoint families
├── registry.py     loads rankings, resolves "best:coding" → (provider, model_id)
└── dispatcher.py   makes the actual HTTP call to Ollama / Groq / OpenRouter

rankings/
├── local.yaml      per-category rankings from own benchmark runs
└── cloud.yaml      per-category rankings from public benchmarks (no live calls)

benchmark/          harness for running your own benchmarks
plans/              roadmap notes (e.g. Nvidia NIM integration)
results/            raw benchmark JSON — historical record
```

---

## Supported Models

The full, current inventory lives in [`models.md`](models.md) — **generated** from
`rankings/cloud.yaml` and `rankings/local.yaml` by `scripts/render_models.py`
(the `/model-scout` daily audit re-renders it; `--check` fails if it is stale).
Cascade order per category is whatever the yaml lists; the slot-0 picks as of
2026-10-01:

| Category | Slot 0 (cloud) | Slot 0 (local, Ollama) |
|---|---|---|
| reasoning, coding, math, summarization, code_debug, context | `nvidia/minimaxai/minimax-m3.1-flash` | `qwen2.5:7b` / `qwen2.5-coder:7b` / `deepseek-r1:8b` |
| instruction | `groq/qwen/qwen3.8-27b` | `qwen2.5:7b` |
| multilingual | `groq/openai/gpt-oss-20b` | `qwen2.5:7b` |
| decisions (`/v1/systemone`) | `typesafe/jev-latest` (needs key) | `qwen3.5:4b` (ollama-chat); `d3:4b-nvfp4` opt-in |

NVIDIA NIM's frontier models hang on a rotating basis (see the dated `NOTE`s in
`rankings/cloud.yaml`); Groq, OpenRouter `:free` and Gemini are the stable backbone.

---
